events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.94)
events.body:
This is a driver-side cancellation in which the driver asserted rider no-show, so the case is routed by NS-0 to NS-1/NS-2 [F4][F11][F12][NS-0]. The $6.61 cancellation fee may only be retained if all three NS-1 elements hold.

Element (i) is satisfied: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 21:29:10 [F6][NS-1]. The single conflicting null timeline entry [F7] is overridden by the tap record and is not relied on by either side [F6][F7][NS-1]. Element (ii) is also satisfied: at the moment of the tap the driver was 42 m from the pickup point, and his closest approach was 38 m [F6][F1][NS-1].

Element (iii) fails. Cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 2 min 50 s [F2], and the cancellation came 2 min 50 s after the platform-recorded arrival and 1 min 45 s after the tap [F5][F6]. Both are short of the required more-than-3-minutes threshold [NS-1]. The driver's statement that he waited at least 5 minutes [F12] is a statement only, and the gps/timeline records [F2][F3][F5] control over it; even the driver's advocate rests solely on the GPS presence facts [F1][F3][F6] and abandons [F12][NS-1]. His stationary period of 2 min 5 s [F3] is likewise below the threshold.

Because NS-1 (iii) is not met, NS-2 applies and the $6.61 recorded cancellation fee is refunded in full [F8][NS-2]. The amount follows the recorded fee, which is the only charge in issue with no surge applied: $6.61 [F8][F9][NS-2].

No account flag is warranted. The additional flag_account step under NS-2 attaches only where the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS shows him outside the pickup radius; here the GPS puts him 42 m away at the tap and 38 m at closest approach, so there was no fake tap [F6][F1][NS-2]. Independently, the driver has no upheld disputes in 90 days, so repeat-abuse account action is not triggered [F17][NS-2]. Profile facts [F16][F17] are not used to decide the merits in either direction [NS-2].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher; no account flag on the driver.

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled as a no-show, but the system GPS record shows the driver was within 200 m of the pickup point for only 2 min 50 s before cancelling, which is below the >3 minute waiting requirement.

The driver's own tap record and movement record contradict a 3-minute wait: the platform logged arrival at 21:28:05 and the driver cancelled at 21:30:55, only 2 min 50 s later — less than three minutes.

The timeline shows the driver did tap "I'm Here", but even counting from the tap at 21:29:10 he stayed within 200 m for only 1 min 45 s before cancelling, so the required >3 minutes of waiting at the pickup was never met.
The driver's written claim of having waited at least 5 minutes is contradicted by the system records and is defeated by them; his stationary period before cancellation was only 2 min 5 s.
Because the NS-1 conditions (arrival at the pickup point plus more than 3 minutes of waiting) are not satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee charged on record must be refunded in full to the rider.

The rider was in the vehicle-hailing process at the stated pickup area and the driver never completed the trip, so no completed-trip waiting fee applies; the only disputed charge is the $6.61 cancellation fee.

The driver's account shows 451 trips in 90 days with no prior disputes, so no finding of repeated abuse is asked for against him; the request is limited to refunding this fee and having the fee-button record reviewed through the normal escalation path.

weaknesses: The driver did tap "I'm Here" (F6) and did chat "I'm here" at 21:29 (F10), so the other side will argue he was genuinely present and the shortfall is only ~10 seconds of waiting (2 min 50 s per F2 vs the >3 min rule).

The rider's own profile shows 2 no-show disputes upheld in 90 days (F16), which the driver may use to argue the rider has a pattern of not showing up, even though profile facts cannot decide the case.
There is no GPS evidence of the rider's own position, so we cannot prove the rider was at the pickup point and ready to board within the wait window.

claims.assertion: The driver reached and remained at the pick-up point: GPS shows his closest approach to the pickup was 38 m at 21:30:00 and he was stationary 21:28:50–21:30:55, 39 m from the pickup (F1, F3), so the 'at the pick-up location' element of NS-1(ii) is met.
The driver indicated arrival in the app: the timeline records an 'I'm Here' tap at 21:29:10 while he was 42 m from the pick-up point (F6), satisfying NS-1(i).
The driver's in-app message 'I'm here, silver Toyota Altis.' at 21:29 corroborates his on-site presence and notice to the rider (F10).

The waiting-time element is not made out on the system records: cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 2 min 50 s (F2) and the cancellation came 2 min 50 s after the recorded arrival (F5), both short of the > 3 minutes required by NS-1(iii).

Because NS-1(iii) fails while (i) and (ii) hold, and the GPS confirms the driver was genuinely inside the pick-up radius when he tapped 'I'm Here', the $6.61 should be refunded to the rider under NS-2 but no account flag for 'I'm Here' abuse is warranted — the arrangement common in NS-2 applies only when the driver was outside the radius.

The driver's written statement that he 'waited at least 5 minutes' (F12) is contradicted by the system records of 2 min 50 s within 200 m (F2, F5), so only the shorter system-recorded period may be used.

The driver cancelled for the stated reason that the rider did not appear (F11, F12), not for an unexplained reason, so this is a no-show-policy case under NS-0/NS-1 rather than driver-side cancellation abuse under NS-3.

The driver has a clean record — 634-day account, rating 4.7, 451 trips in 90 days and zero disputes or upheld complaints (F17) — which supports no account flag being added for this single, near-miss arrival attempt (F17 is profile only, offered as mitigation, not as a finding).

weaknesses: The system records cut against the no-show claim: only 2 min 50 s inside the 200 m radius (F2) and cancellation 2 min 50 s after recorded arrival (F5), so NS-1(iii)'s > 3 minutes is not met on the very facts I rely on for (i) and (ii).

My client's own written statement of a 5-minute wait (F12) is directly contradicted by the GPS/timeline facts (F2, F5), and under the system-records-win rule the rider will use F2/F5/F12 to show the wait was too short.

The rider will also point to NS-4 to argue the arrival came late and to her upheld no-show history as a rider-side credibility point (F16); note F16 relates to the rider's prior disputes, not to my client, and F7 (a null 'I'm Here' field in one timeline record) conflicts with F6 and will likely be read against us.

points.response: Conceded as far as it goes: GPS does put the driver 38–39 m from the pickup point at 21:30:00 and stationary 21:28:50–21:30:55 (F1, F3), so NS-1(ii) is met — but the driver's presence near the point does not supply the missing waiting time.

Conceded on the tap: the timeline records an "I'm Here" tap at 21:29:10 with the driver 42 m from the pickup (F6), satisfying NS-1(i); note F7's null field in another timeline record is outweighed by F6 and is not our best point either.

We do not contest that the driver messaged "I'm here" at 21:29 (F10); a chat message loses to the GPS/timeline records (F2, F5) on how long he actually waited, so it proves notice, not compliance with the 3-minute threshold.

This is the decisive claim and it is ours: the driver never accumulated more than 2 min 50 s within 200 m before cancelling (F2) and cancelled 2 min 50 s after the recorded arrival (F5), so NS-1(iii)'s "more than 3 minutes" is not met and the no-show fee cannot stand.

We agree on refund_full of the $6.61 under NS-2 (F8) and agree no "I'm Here" abuse flag is warranted against the driver here, since the GPS puts him inside the radius when he tapped (F3, F6); that concession does not change the rider's entitlement to the refund.
Agreed: the driver's 5-minute statement (F12) is contradicted by the system records of 2 min 50 s inside 200 m and 2 min 50 s after arrival (F2, F5), and the system records win over the statement.

We accept this is a no-show-policy case under NS-0/NS-1 rather than NS-3, because the driver stated he was cancelling for non-appearance (F11, F12); that routing is exactly what makes NS-2's full refund apply once NS-1(iii) fails (F2, F5).

The driver's clean profile (F17: 634-day account, 4.7 rating, 451 trips, 0 upheld disputes) is not contested and we never sought an account flag against him; under the policy, profile facts cannot be used to defeat the rider's refund entitlement, which follows from the timing records (F2, F5) and NS-2.

Conceded on the arithmetic of NS-1(iii): the system record of 2 min 50 s within 200 m before cancellation (F2) does not exceed 3 minutes, so the driver's no-show cancellation did not satisfy the statutory wait and the $6.61 cannot be retained.

The timing itself is not in dispute (recorded arrival 21:28:05, cancellation 21:30:55 per F5 and F4), but the same records show the driver was at 38–39 m from the pickup and stationary there for the last 2 min 5 s (F1, F3), so this is a near-miss on the wait clock, not a driver who never turned up.

The tap at 21:29:10 while 42 m from the pickup (F6) establishes that NS-1(i) and NS-1(ii) were both satisfied on GPS, so the only failed element is the duration in NS-1(iii) — which matters because NS-2's additional flag_account applies only where the driver pressed 'I'm Here' while outside the pickup radius, and F6 shows he was inside it.

Agreed: my client's statement of a 5-minute wait (F12) is defeated by the system records of 2 min 50 s within 200 m and 2 min 5 s stationary (F2, F3), so I do not rely on F12 and rest only on the GPS presence facts (F1, F3, F6).
The refund of the $6.61 recorded on the fare record (F8) follows from NS-2 and I do not contest the amount, which is the only charge in issue.

Correct that no completed-trip waiting fee arises — the ride was never completed, only the $6.61 cancellation fee appears on the fare record with no surge (F8, F9), so NS-6 and the $5.00 waiting fee are not engaged in this case.

The driver's clean record — 634-day account, 451 trips in 90 days, zero disputes or upheld complaints (F17) — supports closing this as a single shortfall of about ten seconds with no account flag, rather than escalating it as abuse; the rider's own profile showing 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F16) is not offered as a finding, since profile facts cannot decide the case.
